name: Balpakram National Park
description: National park in South Garo Hills known as the 'Land of Perpetual Winds' or 'Land of Spirits' in Garo folklore. Features dramatic canyons, plateaus, gorges, and dense forests. Home to elephants, red pandas, clouded leopards, wild water buffalo, and diverse birds. Part of UNESCO tentative Garo Hills Conservation Area.
facts: Requires permit for entry; best Oct-March

name: Siju Cave (Dobakkol / Bat Cave)
description: One of India's longest limestone caves (about 4.7 km surveyed), famous for stalactites, stalagmites, underground streams, and large bat colonies. Located near Simsang River; popular for adventure exploration with local guides. Significant for biospeleology research.
facts: Third or among longest caves in India
About 30 km from Baghmara, 125 km from Tura
Guide essential; best Nov-March; entry fee low

name: Wari Chora
description: Hidden river canyon in South Garo Hills with turquoise waters of the Rongdik River flowing between tall limestone cliffs. Ideal for boating, kayaking, trekking, and photography in a remote, uncrowded setting. Name refers to 'land of the seven serpents' in local lore.
facts: Near Emangre village, about 2 hours from Baghmara
Requires off-road vehicle and local guide for last stretch
Part of emerging Siju-Wari Chora-Baghmara circuit

name: Baghmara Pitcher Plant Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Small protected sanctuary near Baghmara town dedicated to the endangered endemic pitcher plant Nepenthes khasiana (locally Me'mang-Koksi). Located in reserve forest on the India-Bangladesh border area, with dense vegetation and occasional wildlife.
facts: Also known as Baghmara Reserve Forest

name: Baghmara Town
description: District headquarters of South Garo Hills, a gateway town on the Simsang River near the Bangladesh border. Base for exploring Balpakram, Siju Cave, and Wari Chora. Known for local markets, Garo culture, and as entry to border reserve forests.
facts: Name from legend of tiger killed by local hero
Connected by road to Tura and Guwahati

name: Siju Bird Sanctuary
description: Small sanctuary across the Simsang River from Siju Cave, known for birdwatching including hornbills and peacock pheasants. Quiet riverside location ideal for early morning visits amid the Garo Hills forests.
facts: Near Siju Cave and Napak Lake
Good for migratory and resident birds

name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills district, a colonial-era hill station known for its pine forests, lakes, markets, and cool climate. Base for exploring waterfalls, caves, and living root bridges of the Khasi Hills.
facts: Named after the deity Lei Shyllong
Connected by road to Guwahati (~100 km)
Known for golf course, music culture, and local cuisine

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at about 1,965 m, offering panoramic views of Shillong city, surrounding hills, and distant plains. Features a viewpoint near an Air Force radar station; requires ID for entry.
facts: Highest peak in the state ~1,965 m

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall near Shillong, locally known as Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew. Cascades through lush greenery; popular short stop for visitors.

name: Ward's Lake
description: Man-made lake in the heart of Shillong, locally called Nan Polok, with gardens, footpaths, and boating. Named after a British chief commissioner; popular evening spot.

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Famous for being one of the wettest places on Earth, located on the southern edge of the Khasi Hills plateau. Gateway to major waterfalls, caves, and living root bridges.
facts: Base for Nohkalikai, Mawsmai, root bridges

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India at about 340 m, dropping from the Sohra plateau into a turquoise pool. Associated with a local legend of a woman named Likai.
facts: Best during monsoon for full flow

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Segmented waterfall with seven streams cascading ~315 m over limestone cliffs near Mawsmai. Spectacular during monsoon; views of Bangladesh plains from the viewpoint.
facts: Also called Seven Sisters or Mawsmai Falls

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Accessible limestone cave near Sohra with illuminated passages, stalactites, and stalagmites. Short ~150 m route suitable for beginners.
facts: Lit for tourists; some tight spots

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Known as Asia's cleanest village, with bamboo dustbins, floral pathways, and community hygiene practices. Features a skywalk and nearby living root bridge; matrilineal Khasi culture.
facts: Awarded cleanest in Asia by Discover India 2003
About 90 km from Shillong near Bangladesh border

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Iconic two-tier living root bridge in Nongriat village, grown from Ficus elastica roots by Khasi communities over centuries. Requires a strenuous descent of ~3,500 steps from Tyrna.
facts: UNESCO tentative Jingkieng Jri cultural landscape

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic canyon and viewpoint near Smit, offering expansive views of valleys and hills. Meaning 'end of hills'; popular for photography and short treks.
facts: About 25 km from Shillong via Smit

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Protected sacred grove preserved by Khasi traditional beliefs, with ancient trees, monoliths, and biodiversity. Guided walks available; entry regulated.

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures
description: Museum in Mawlai, Shillong showcasing the cultures, lifestyles, and artefacts of Northeast India's indigenous peoples. Seven-storey structure with extensive exhibits.
